production.caller: Scene::validate and Scene::apply_one before an Insert

specification: For any tree and any set obeying the IdentitySet contract, against the preorder identity sequence (for the insertion check, the tree followed by the inserted subtree): Ok holds only when no identity repeats and none was already in the set, and the set is then exactly the old set plus the sequence. DuplicateNode(d) names the first repeating position k: the prefix before k is unrepeated, d is in the old set or in that prefix, and the set is exactly the old set plus the prefix. No other error is produced.
assumptions: The IdentitySet contract: admit reports whether the identity was absent and adds it. The BTreeSet instance of this contract is tested, not proved.
Callers pass an empty set; that is by reading, the specification is stated for any starting set.

Verus+Z3.model_note: Canvas, Style, Semantics and Point are replaced in the proof by value types the kernel cannot read. In the proof copy the Ok arm of check_insert_identities binds the second call to a local so a proof block can follow it; the call is the same.

Proptest.includes: Arbitrary trees up to 24 nodes, an inserted subtree from the same spec and an optional seeded identity, with the production BTreeSet instance wrapped to record the order asked, against an independent recursive preorder and a linear scan for the first repeat. Identities are in a small domain so repeats occur.

Loom.reason: The kernel holds no shared state and no synchronization primitive; the set is taken by &mut and the tree by shared reference with no interior mutability in the fields read.
Loom.substitute_evidence: None added: the compiler's borrow rule is the argument. It is not a concurrency proof.

real_path_test.mutation_checked: Six manual mutations, one run each, not in the Verus control table: children pushed in forward order, subtree checked before the tree, Insert check removed, admit always reporting new, separate sets for tree and subtree, subtree skipped. Each failed the new unit test or another scene unit test.

behavior_change_note: collect_unique_ids became generic over IdentitySet. vec![root] became new and push, while let became loop with match, and extend over reversed children became a descending index loop. The two calls in apply_one moved into check_insert_identities. The visiting order, the sets and the errors should be unchanged; that equivalence with the old text is argued by reading and tests, not proved. The BTreeSet is still created at the same point, per check.
